title: Sickness Unto Death
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Eighteen-year-old psychology student Futaba Kazuma takes lodging in a gloomy mansion in exchange for caring for Emiru, a young woman whose despair has turned her hair white and left her body near death; he falls for her and tries to pull her out of it (blurb via AniList and MangaUpdates; Manga Bookshelf review). The story opens with the adult Kazuma at her grave and unfolds in flashback over two volumes, with repressed memories and a split personality in its mystery (MangaUpdates).
life_message: It suggests that despair is a real sickness that love alone cannot cure, and that helpers must respect limits (to verify).

content.note: Attempted murder listed (MangaUpdates); not described in review (to verify).
Reviewer calls it 'watching a car crash in slow motion'; creepy mansion, dying heroine, grave opening (review; AniList Tragedy 79%).
Caregiver-patient romance becomes 'more intimate' (review); MangaUpdates lists Adult genre and Borderline H, AniList Nudity 73%; explicitness unverified (to verify).
Despair and depression as a deadly illness, split personality, heroine's death (review; MangaUpdates Depression, Mental Illness, Dying Protagonist).
Student crosses therapist-patient boundaries; reviewer calls this a serious mistake (review; MangaUpdates Doctor-Patient Relationship).

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese seinen psychological drama, with a reserved household and a teacher whose authority goes unchallenged.

delivery.evidence: Kazuma's teacher explains Emiru's mindset in the abstract (review); otherwise not called preachy (to verify).

delivery.note: The series explains its psychology through a teacher figure while dramatizing it through Emiru.

winners_losers: No one clearly wins: Emiru dies and Kazuma is left to reflect; the reviewer faults his choices. Sympathy goes to the suffering heroine.
